## Question and scope

Explain the submitted systems' differences using frozen organizer question-level results, rather than creating new predictions. This is a descriptive, post-hoc paper analysis, not a new experiment or a selection policy evaluated prospectively. Primary topic: answer ranking and evidence selection. The paired counts here are the evidence-of-record for the paper's added analysis.

## Evidence and verification

Read original `NP_Labs-MC.zip`, `NP_Labs.zip`, and `vqa.mcq.scores.txt` from revision `3efb5b19dbd6d8d59232986cc25ef049af24ba5e`, under `docs/experiments/artifacts/trec-vqa-2026-official-results/`. No checkout change, inference, or scorer rerun. Aggregate evidence is in [question-level-analysis.json](question-level-analysis.json).

The four MC files align on 2,428 question IDs, have the same official correct answer per question, and match the testing question file's video IDs. Correct totals reproduce 1,912, 2,025, 2,052, and 2,047. Under Unicode NFKC and collapsed-whitespace matching, every organizer correct answer appears at its reported rank in each of the four tracked revised-option submission files. This checks availability in the submitted ranking, not an independent reconstruction of the original options or semantic correctness of the ground truth. The original leaderboard lists a maximum 2,058 correct, or 84.7611%; our best has six fewer and is second by top-1 accuracy.

AG comparisons use rank-one scores in the all-references mode over 2,428 scored rows. Recomputed means reproduce the workbook at its published precision. Comparisons count higher/equal/lower metric values; they do not turn similarity scores into binary correctness. Scores were already frozen before this analysis.

## Observed results

MC3 versus MC1: 219 incorrect-to-correct changes, 79 correct-to-incorrect changes, net +140. MC3 has 376 misses. All four MC runs miss 271 rows; 58 have the MC1/MC2 wrong and MC3/MC4 correct pattern.

Qwen dual-view versus Gemini fusion: BERTScore higher/equal/lower = 1,284/27/1,117; METEOR = 609/144/1,675; STS = 1,035/43/1,350. Qwen improves mean METEOR and BERTScore over the frame baseline, but not STS. There is no universal AG winner.

## Earlier selected cases and selection boundary (superseded presentation)

Guiding case: internal question 1237. Selected from the 58-row MC rescue pattern after reading short-question candidates, also checking that Qwen outranks fusion on all three AG metrics. It asks for a general definition; Qwen gives one while Gemini supplies a specific story detail. Paper figures paraphrase the question and answer meanings, preserving original official scores and MC outcomes. That earlier draft included no copied frames, full options, or verbatim question strings; the explicitly authorized shared-case revision below supersedes this boundary.

Option-overlap case: internal question 2092. Selected from MC1-correct/MC3-wrong rows. The official meaning is passage along a route; MC3 selects slow movement. The descriptions can coexist, making it a candidate annotation/option-overlap issue, not a confirmed bad label. Video and annotation review has not been performed.

## Interpretation and limits

Evidence validity: valid descriptive comparison of the archived scored panel. Decision: explain both improvements and regressions in the paper; no router or model is promoted. Case selection is post-hoc and illustrative, not representative. The earlier draft kept exact test strings and private media outside the report; the user later explicitly authorized selected actual examples in the local draft. A selected answer-scope mismatch supports a local interpretation, not a prevalence claim. Similarity differences can reflect wording. We cannot attribute model errors to perception, speech, or training without additional evidence. Correct-option availability does not establish that annotations are unambiguous. No significance test was run.

## Next action

Author review of the paraphrased cases and paper. If causal failure claims or dataset-quality claims are needed, inspect the corresponding videos and adjudicate the competing option meanings before strengthening them.

## Question-opening analysis

Post-hoc, mutually exclusive groups use lowercased question text, collapsed whitespace, stripped leading quote characters, and word-boundary matches for `how many`, `why`, `when`, `where`, and `what sound`. Everything else is Other. These are lexical groups, not comprehensive semantic task categories. The grouping was chosen after inspecting common openings; it is descriptive, not a preregistered hypothesis test. No category-specific model was selected or rerun. Group sizes sum to 2,428 and correct counts reproduce every official MC total. Per-group counts are saved in the JSON evidence.

MC3: How many 200/309, Why 312/360, When 67/72, Where 73/90, What sound 31/35, Other 1,369/1,562. How-many rows make up 12.7% of questions and 29.0% of MC3 errors (109/376). MC2 gets 205/309, so full review is not better on this group despite being better overall. This identifies a weakness under the official scoring; it does not establish a visual-counting mechanism. Some reference options are broad quantity terms that can overlap exact-number options. No confidence or significance claims are made for subgroup comparisons.

Additional selected case IDs: 2161 (count disagreement), 2021 (specific intent versus insufficient information), and 1220 (vessel versus surrounding location). Each has all four runs wrong under official scoring. Paper descriptions paraphrase the questions/options, omit private media, and distinguish possible mechanisms from verified outcomes. Cases were selected from short-question MC3 misses after observing the category counts; they are not an independently sampled failure-prevalence panel.

## Follow-up visual inspection — 2026-10-05

For selected counting case 2161, inspected a contact sheet sampled at 1 fps across the full 9.568-second local source video. One solid-pink disk, one rainbow disk, and a reversible multicolored toy are visible. Official answer is one; MC1, MC2, and MC3 choose three; MC4 chooses two. Interpretation: the prediction matches the total toy count rather than the solid-pink subset; because the other toys contain pink too, broad color interpretation remains a competing explanation. This supports a case-specific color-filtering issue, not a proven cause of all counting errors. At this inspection stage frames were not embedded; the later user-authorized figure now embeds selected local frames. No audio adjudication was performed; the paper removes the uninspected sound example and reports audio-related groups only as lexical score groups. Also inspected action-case frames, but did not use them to establish intent. Earlier statements that no videos were inspected are superseded for this counting case only.

## Counting follow-up and grouping decision

The released question JSON contains Q_ID, Video_ID, and Question, with no task-type annotation. Retained reproducible lexical groups rather than substituting unvalidated semantic categories. A richer methodology would independently annotate reasoning task, required evidence, and error mechanism; those annotations have not been completed for this panel.

On the 309 how-many rows, MC3 corrects 24 MC1 errors and loses 21 MC1 successes (net +3). All four miss 79; 30 of MC3's 109 misses are correct in at least one other run. Counts calculated directly from archived Top_1 fields on the same question IDs.

Inspected case 106 at 1 fps across the local clip: two people visible; MC1/2/3 choose 4, MC4 chooses 2, official 2. Added a 4-second frame under prior explicit authorization for actual examples. Cause of overcount not established. Case 108: all choose 'A crowd', official 'Many'; compatible quantity descriptions, not a verified perception failure. Cases distinguish precise numeric disagreement, counting-criterion interpretation, and option overlap without claiming an exhaustive taxonomy. Selection is post-hoc. Case 185 frames were also inspected but not promoted into the paper because playing-versus-presence remains ambiguous.

## Explicit numeric disagreements and correct-identification score gap

Replaced the Spider-Man discussion as the main failure example. Across MC3's 109 misses in the 309-row case-insensitive word-boundary how-many group, 76 have a different explicit integer in selected and official options. Normalization strips whitespace/lowercases; accepts digit-only integers or whole number words zero through twenty. No extraction from sentences, ranges, or vague quantities. This is a reproducible output-disagreement family, not 76 video-adjudicated perception failures. Selected inspected case106 supports the official count, with AG1=2, AG2=1, AG3/4=4; official AG scores show that the incorrect short numeral1 receives BERTScore .999798.

Inspected case853 video at1fps: a cockroach image appears (with a humorous face overlay). Official MC answer Cockroach. AG1/2 answer cockroach; AG3/4 answer The bug in the video is a cockroach. Per-answer all-reference STS/METEOR/BERT = 1/.5/.975272 versus .587251/.277778/.815225. Same identification, lower scores for longer wording; no prevalence claim. Embedded local frame at6s under existing user authorization. Candidate207 was inspected but rejected: background people complicate the official count, so it is not a clean correctness case.
